# Assignment Overview

This group assignment documents the process used to download the Wellness Ranch survey responses from Qualtrics and prepare the data for statistical analysis in SPSS.

The assignment has two parts:

1. Review, clean, and download the raw survey data from Qualtrics.
2. Prepare the data in SPSS and document all transformations in a syntax file.

The final SPSS deliverables are:

- A cleaned SPSS data file with the `.sav` extension
- An SPSS syntax file with the `.sps` extension

# Part 2: SPSS Data Preparation

## Data-Preparation Checklist

The group used the following checklist to prepare the SPSS dataset:

- [ ] Preserve an unchanged copy of the original raw data.
- [ ] Remove preview and test responses.
- [ ] Review incomplete and duplicate responses.
- [ ] Confirm that each row represents one respondent.
- [ ] Confirm that each column represents one variable.
- [ ] Assign the correct measurement level to each variable.
- [ ] Add clear variable labels.
- [ ] Add value labels to nominal and ordinal variables.
- [ ] Identify missing-value codes.
- [ ] Convert “not applicable” or similar responses to missing values when appropriate.
- [ ] Identify and reverse-code negatively worded items.
- [ ] Run reliability analysis for multi-item constructs.
- [ ] Conduct factor analysis where appropriate.
- [ ] Create composite variables for reliable multi-item constructs.
- [ ] Save every transformation in the SPSS syntax file.
- [ ] Review the cleaned dataset for errors.
- [ ] Save the final `.sav` and `.sps` files.

## Measurement Levels

Measurement levels were assigned using the group’s Construct and Measurement Table.

| Variable Type | SPSS Measure | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| Unordered categories | Nominal | Gender, city, device, insurance type |
| Ordered categories | Ordinal | Age group, education, income, search frequency |
| Likert-scale and composite measures | Scale | Trust, clarity, inquiry intention, donation intention |

## Variable and Value Labels

The group reviewed the imported variable names and labels in SPSS Variable View.

Variable labels were revised so that each variable could be understood without referring back to the Qualtrics questionnaire. Value labels were added for nominal and ordinal variables.

Examples include:

| Variable | Example Variable Label | Example Value Labels |
|---|---|---|
| `Q2` | Inland Empire residency | 1 = Yes; 2 = No; 3 = Not sure |
| `Q3` | Searched online for wellness services | 1 = Yes; 2 = No |
| `Q18` | Primary device used for online search | 1 = Smartphone; 2 = Computer; 3 = Tablet |
| `Q21` | Age category | 1 = 18–24; 2 = 25–34; etc. |

## Missing Values

The group reviewed the dataset for responses such as:

- No opinion
- Not applicable
- Prefer not to say
- Blank responses
- Questions hidden through Qualtrics display logic

The group determined whether each response should remain as a valid category or be coded as system missing. All missing-value decisions were documented in the SPSS syntax file.

## Reverse-Coded Items

The questionnaire contains the following negatively worded item:

| Variable | Statement | Required Action |
|---|---|---|
| `ATT3` | I usually skip sponsored ads and scroll to regular results. | Reverse-code before creating the attitude composite |

For a seven-point scale, the reverse-coded value is calculated as:

\[
\text{ATT3R} = 8 - \text{ATT3}
\]

A new variable named `ATT3R` should be created so that the original response remains unchanged.

The reverse-coded item should be checked to confirm that higher values have the same conceptual meaning as the other items in the construct.

## Composite Variables

Composite variables will be created only after the corresponding items demonstrate acceptable reliability and an appropriate factor structure.

Composite variables will generally be calculated using the mean of the retained items. Using the mean preserves the original response scale and allows easier interpretation.

Example:

```spss
COMPUTE ATT_MEAN = MEAN(ATT1, ATT2, ATT3R).
EXECUTE.
```

All composite-variable calculations will be saved in the SPSS syntax file.

# SPSS Syntax Documentation

All modifications must be recorded in the `.sps` file.

The syntax file should include:

- Variable and value labels
- Missing-value definitions
- Reverse coding
- Attention-check handling
- Reliability analyses
- Factor analyses
- Composite-variable calculations
- Case exclusions
- Any additional transformations

The team will use **Paste** instead of **OK** when running SPSS procedures so that the corresponding syntax is preserved.
